hypothesis: Solo practices on Open Dental will pay 300 USD a month for an AI receptionist that books appointments after hours

landing.name: NightDesk
landing.headline: Never miss an after-hours patient call again
landing.subhead: An AI receptionist that answers your practice's phone at night and books the appointment in your calendar.
bullets: Sends you a morning summary of every call

interview.who: Dentists or office managers in solo or 2-chair practices that use Open Dental
questions: Tell me about the last time a patient called after hours. What happened?
How do you handle calls when the front desk is busy today?
How many calls do you think you miss in a week, and how do you know?
What have you tried to fix it, and what did it cost?
Who decides on new tools for the practice, and how did the last purchase go?
red_flags: They don't know how many calls they miss
They already use the booking line of their calendar tool and are happy with it

outreach.text: Hi Dr. Smith, I'm testing an after-hours phone assistant for practices on Open Dental. Could I ask you 5 questions about how you handle calls at night? 15 minutes, no sales pitch.
Question for practice owners: how do you handle patient calls after 6 pm? I'm researching this for a small project and would love to hear what works for you.

targets.label: Practices that pay the 300 EUR pilot deposit

kill_criteria: Fewer than 1 paid pilot out of 10 calls by 2026-11-19: archive

entries.evidence: 10 calls, 2 interested, nobody paid the deposit

moves.why: Cold email got a 27% reply rate

gross_margin.note: ~49% margin (estimate): $101 voice, PMS API, fees on $199. R5 cap: costs_eat_margin hit (2.5 -> 2).

pricing_power.note: $199 undercuts $299-$899 dental tools; generic Quo Sona tops out at $199. Price is the only lever.

build_effort.note: Voice API + Open Dental slot/booking API: ~4-6 weeks at 10 h/week; HIPAA setup on top.

skills_match.note: Developer covers the build; dental workflows, HIPAA and B2B sales are new.

capital_needed.note: $2,000 covers a pilot on Open Dental; Dentrix write access costs $10,000 one-time.

time_to_mvp.note: First paid pilot ~8 weeks out (estimate): build, BAA, per-practice PMS access.

sales_cycle.note: Dentist demo, trust in an AI touching the schedule, PMS vendor access: weeks per deal.

channel_readiness.note: No audience; cold outreach only. Dental clicks average $7.85; ADA channel taken by Weave.

trend.note: +86% YoY search growth for 'AI receptionist' (DataForSEO via FindSkill, 2026).

free_alternatives.note: Quo includes 10 free AI calls/month; Weave bundles it. Free covers part, not PMS booking.

competitor_density.note: 20+ direct competitors found: Weave, Arini, Flossy, Dentina, Viva, TensorLinks, SmileDial...

differentiation.note: Only a lower price. 'I am a developer' is not an edge buyers see.

legal_regulatory.note: PHI on calls: BAAs needed across telephony, LLM, TTS and storage; TCPA for AI-voice callbacks.

platform_dependency.note: Depends on PMS API access per practice and on one voice-AI vendor's pricing.

market_risk.note: Durable need: 55% of dentists find admin hiring extremely/very hard (ADA HPI, 2025).

skills.note: Builds software; no dental, healthcare compliance or sales track record stated.

assets.note: No audience, dental network or data stated.

interest.note: Goal stated as side income; no domain interest stated.
